# linux_ssh_authorized_key (Resource)

Authorizes a public key to log in as a user, in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, like Ansible's `authorized_key`. The `.ssh` directory and the file are created with the right owner and permissions when needed. Other keys are left untouched.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_ssh_authorized_key" "alice" {
  user = linux_user.alice.name
  key  = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
}

# With options.
resource "linux_ssh_authorized_key" "backup" {
  user = "root"
  key  = "from=\"10.0.0.0/8\",no-pty ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKYAXtawxjduXikR6hHbQt+T+A5fnGDqaZFNP3iFfjIC backup@vault"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Public key, as a line of `authorized_keys`: optional options, key type, base64 key and optional comment, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA... alice@laptop`.
- `user` (String) User the key logs in as.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) User and fingerprint of the key.
- `path` (String) Path of the `authorized_keys` file.
